extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for the Spencer Foundation Small Research Grants on Education (PIs and Co-PIs; academic researchers at nonprofit or public institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and submitting a field-initiated research proposal to the Spencer Foundation's Small Research Grants on Education program (projects up to $50,000, 1–5 years), following the program's eligibility, content, formatting, and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose and emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Support rigorous, intellectually ambitious and technically sound research that is relevant to the most pressing questions and compelling opportunities in education; field-initiated proposals across disciplines and methods that develop new foundational knowledge with lasting impact on educational discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is open to work across learning contexts (classroom, workplace, family, community, playing field), disciplines (e.g., education, anthropology, philosophy, psychology, sociology, law, economics, history, neuroscience), and methods (quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods, ethnographies, computational modeling, design-based research, participatory methods, historical research). Spencer values creative, open-minded scholarship, deep inquiry, and robust questions; projects may incorporate multiple data sources, span sufficient time for depth, and/or work closely with practitioners or community members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible project type — must be research on education
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be for research projects that aim to study education. Proposals for activities other than research are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of ineligible proposals include program evaluations with no significant research component, creation of professional development programs, curricula, and/or assessment tools with no significant research component, scholarships, capital projects, and software development. Likewise, research focused on areas other than education is not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator and Co-PI qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-PIs must have an earned doctorate in an academic discipline or professional field. Graduate students may be part of the team but may not be named PI or Co-PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI must be affiliated with a non-profit organization or public/governmental institution that will serve as the administering organization if awarded. Examples: non-profit or public colleges, universities, school districts, research facilities, and other 501(c)(3) non-profits (or equivalent outside the U.S.). Spencer does not award grants directly to individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and budget currency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals must be submitted in English and budgets must be proposed in U.S. dollars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget limit and indirect costs policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed budgets are limited to $50,000 total and may not include indirect cost charges per Spencer’s policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible investigators may also request supplemental course release funds (see separate rubric) which can raise total requested funds up to $60,000 if awarded. The $50,000 cap applies to the Small Grant budget itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects proposed may not be longer than 5 years in duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent Spencer grant/proposal restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-PIs may only hold one active research grant from the Spencer Foundation at a time and may not submit more than one research proposal to Spencer at a time across specified programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction covers Small Grants, Large Grants, Racial Equity Research Grants, and Research-Practice Partnership Program. If an applicant has another proposal under review, they must wait for a final decision before submitting a new proposal. Exception: Spencer Vision Grants — PIs/Co-PIs may apply for a Vision Grant while holding/awaiting other Spencer grants or proposals, but the Vision Grant project must be distinct from other Spencer projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Personnel section requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the online application, the person creating the draft is automatically assigned as PI; Co-PIs may be added after they follow required steps. The application also requires confirmation that neither PI nor Co-PIs currently have another research proposal under review at Spencer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Summary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide project title, start and end dates, central research question(s), and a 200-word project summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary is part of the online application fields (200 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and budget justification structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget form is divided into categories (Salaries, Benefits, Other Collaborator, Travel, Equipment and Software, Project Expenses, Other, Subcontracts) with specific line-item choices; each expense should be added and accompanied by a budget narrative description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcontracts require a separate subcontract budget form per subcontract with the same categories. Detailed guidelines are available within the application form. Use the appropriate Supplemental Course Release line items if requesting that funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Narrative content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a proposal narrative PDF that includes: a description of the project, the central research question(s), the project's significance; a rationale including (a) summary of relevant literature and relationship to that literature and expected contribution to improvement of education, and (b) summary of conceptual framework/theory guiding the project; a description of proposed research methods, participants, data collection instruments, and modes of analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, include: information about proposed sample/case definition and selection procedures; research design and context; description of key constructs, measures and data sources; procedures for data collection; procedures for data analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Narrative formatting and length restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative may not exceed 1800 words and at its conclusion should include the word count in parentheses. The text should be double–spaced and in 12-point font. APA style is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References should follow the narrative in the same PDF and will not count toward the 1800-word limit. Tables and figures can be included in the text where appropriate (used sparingly). The text contained in tables and figures will not count towards the word limit; however, you must describe or explain any tables or figures in the narrative portion (which will contribute to the word count). Proposals that exceed the word limit will not be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI Agreement and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must acknowledge that they have read, understood, and agree to comply with the Spencer Foundation's policy guidelines on responsible and ethical use of generative AI when submitting the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details and the acknowledgement are handled within the online portal; applicants should review the AI policy guidelines in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Timeline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a project timeline as a PDF no more than 1 page in 12-point font indicating proposed start and end dates and key project events and milestones; major activities listed should be reflected in the proposal narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed project duration can be up to 5 years. Teams should plan to begin their project timeline no sooner than 8 months from the original proposal submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Team document requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a project team document (PDF) not exceeding 250 words, double–spaced in 12-point font, identifying roles, responsibilities, and knowledge base of PI, Co-PIs, and supporting researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Co-PIs and supporting researchers are included, articulate how the team will work together and what each member contributes; optionally include a short description of the relationship between the project team and the research site. This document will be reviewed along with PI/Co-PI CVs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional Supplemental Course Release eligibility and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators may request supplemental course release funds up to $10,000 over and above the $50,000 Small Grant budget limit (total up to $60,000) to support course release for the scholar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible the scholar (PI or Co-PI) must have a course load of 6 or above per academic year. Supplemental funds cannot be used for anything besides a course release and should be the standard rate at the institution. Only one additional course release per grant may be requested. Requesting does not guarantee award. If the scholar's course load is less than 6, a course release may still be included but the total budget may not exceed $50,000 and the extra supporting documents are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Course Release required documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: To request supplemental course release funds, include: (1) the amount requested and brief budget narrative in the Proposal Budget (use appropriate Supplemental Course Release line items), (2) a 250-word Course Release Rationale Statement PDF explaining how the additional course release will impact the proposed project, and (3) a Supporting Letter from the scholar's Dean or Chair PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supporting Letter must include: (a) confirmation that the scholar's course load is 6 courses or more per academic year, (b) confirmation that the scholar will be released from teaching a course if awarded the supplemental funds, and (c) confirmation the budgeted amount for the course release is appropriate for their institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission portal and supplemental resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and the full Request for Proposals (including optional appendices, review process, FAQs, and writing guides) must be submitted via Spencer's online portal: https://spencer.smartsimple.us/ .
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the portal to access detailed guidelines and to upload required documents. Deadlines and portal status are posted there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting enforcement and refusal to review overlength proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that exceed specified word limits or do not follow formatting instructions will not be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: narrative >1800 words will not be reviewed; timeline must not exceed 1 page; project team document must not exceed 250 words; specified fonts and spacing (12-pt, double-spaced) should be used.
